model: TUUB Series universal wall-mount controller (Modbus RTU)
equipment_type: Thermostat / heat pump and unitary controller
applies_to: Neptronic TUUB Series universal wall-mount controllers with Modbus, guide TUUB-Modbus Guide-250829 (V1.13).
summary: The TUUB is the larger Neptronic universal wall-mount controller, with four analog outputs, seven binary outputs and four universal inputs, plus options for heat pump and emergency-heat operation. Its Modbus RTU holding registers cover temperatures, humidity, CO2, pressure, light and VOC readings, ramp demands, output states, mode, fan and setpoint control, VFD loops, 6-way valve settings and the configuration set.

addressing.note: Each row prints both the protocol (wire) address, starting at 0, and the 40001-style notation; e.g. 40046 is protocol address 45. The documented field holds the 4xxxx notation.

source.title: TUUB Series Universal Wall-Mount Controller Modbus Communication Module User Guide

notes: Every register is a 16-bit holding register (function 03 to read, 06 or 16 to write); there are no 32-bit values.

Temperatures, setpoints, bands and offsets are reported in °C or °F according to the "temperature unit in Modbus" bit of the system-options register; scaling is x100 for sensor readings and offsets and x10 for setpoints and bands, as listed per register.
Register 0 packs the Neptronic product ID in the high byte and the Modbus address in the low byte.
Left out: the four product-name registers (two ASCII characters each, byte order not spelled out) and every register the guide marks Reserved.

Left out: pulse output values 40185-40191 (data-type column and range text give different scales), the delta-temperature registers 40192-40193, 40100 (analog output 3 ramp, an option list printed with Scale 10) and the floating output values 40182-40183 (Scale 10 in the data-type column but Value x 1 in the range text).
The UI3 signal register (40085) is kept without its option list because the guide numbers two options as 1.
The guide's remarks next to the system-mode values point at register numbers that do not match the table; only the value list is kept.
System option 2 (40046) bit 12 is printed twice in the guide (binary output 7 direction and fan speed option), so that bit is left undefined here.

integration.summary: Read holding registers with function 03 at the wire address shown in the guide's Protocol Address column (Modicon 40001 = address 0). Set the temperature unit for Modbus first, then use the mode, fan and setpoint registers for control.
integration.enable: Modbus is the controller's native protocol; set the address (1-246) and, if needed, a fixed baud rate and parity from the device menu or registers 0-2.
quirks: The guide prints both the 0-based protocol address and the 40001-style notation, so there is no off-by-one guesswork.
Baud register holds baud/100 (384 = 38400); 0 means automatic baud detection.
setup: RS-485 two-wire, RTU. Supported baud rates 9600, 19200, 38400 and 57600; automatic baud detection is the default.
Parity/stop bits come from the communication-port register: 1 = none + 2 stop, 2 = even + 1 stop, 3 = odd + 1 stop.
gotchas: Changing the Modbus temperature-unit bit changes the meaning of every temperature register at once.
Some registers only apply to models with a humidity, CO2 or other optional sensor.
